hypothesis: Iter 78 = JOINT AUXILIARY-SIGNAL OPTIMIZATION (the structural fix deferred from iter 77). CONTEXT: iter 77 (honest benchmark + insulin/lactate/hepatic level anchors) NEVER TESTED ITS OWN HYPOTHESIS — it NaN-aborted at phase-1 epoch 39/50, before phase 2 where the anchors engage and before any benchmark report was written. Root cause from the abort dump: the postprandial_recovery aux signal's 480-step rollout ran away (recovery glucose 100->303 mg/dL; its loss went 0.009->0.70->116.9 over epochs 35-38) and backprop through that unstable rollout produced NaN grads in 113/159 params, which the strict safe_step killed the run on. The main trajectory signal stayed healthy (~0.19) the whole time — the disease is entirely in the auxiliary steps. WHY STRUCTURAL: every one of the ~10 auxiliary/constraint signals took its OWN backward + clip_grad_norm_(10) + optimizer.step() in sequence, so each epoch the model took ~10 independent clipped steps in fighting directions. That (a) ERASES each signal's weight whenever its grad-norm exceeds the clip — the reason 30 iters of weight sweeps went byte-identical (see dead-pathways.md) — and (b) lets one signal both fight the others and unilaterally walk the model into an unstable regime and abort the run. FIX (one structural change, no knob): auxiliary signals now ACCUMULATE their already-weighted gradient (accumulate_grad / finalize_aux_accumulation in safe_step.py — backward only, no solo clip/step/zero), and the trainer applies ONE joint_aux_step (clip_grad_norm_ + step) over the COMBINED aux gradient per epoch. Weights then COMPOSE (the joint clip scales the whole, so relative magnitudes survive), signals stop fighting sequentially, and per-epoch aux drift drops from ~10 clipped steps to one — exactly the drift that drove iter 77's runaway. The trajectory signal keeps its own per-window SGD (the main data fit, ~84 steps/epoch; folding it in would cut its steps ~90x and be untrainable). The two signals that already accumulated internally (cohort, physiology_rules — per-spec/rule backward then a manual clip+step, their iter-67/68 memory pattern) just defer their step to the joint one. ROBUSTNESS (isolation policy): a single aux signal whose loss or gradient is non-finite has its contribution rolled back to a pre-signal grad snapshot and DROPPED (logged [SKIP-NONFINITE]), not aborted — so no single unstable aux rollout can ever again kill a run before it produces numbers; strict abort is preserved for the trajectory signal and, defense-in-depth, for the combined gradient in joint_aux_step. CONFIG HELD IDENTICAL to iter 77 on purpose: this isolates the optimizer-structure change so its effect is attributable, and it FINALLY lets iter 77's honest benchmark + level anchors reach phase 2 and emit the baseline numbers that were the whole point. Any constraint-strength retuning (the joint clip gives all aux signals combined the budget one signal had alone) is a follow-up against that now-real baseline, not bundled here.
expectedEffect: PRIMARY (the bar iter 77 never cleared): the run completes both phases without a NaN abort and writes a benchmark-report.json. With that: (1) per_marker_by_source['real'] skill_vs_persistence for glucose/hr/sbp/dbp/temp recorded as the first honest baseline (glucose skill is a HARD bar — persistence ~0.014 — so near-zero/negative is the honest truth, not a regression); (2) overall_weighted_mape_by_source split real vs teacher; (3) textbook_mean_pass_rate now that its gate is live at 0.45. SECONDARY (iter 77's deferred mechanism, now actually exercised in phase 2): insulin per-marker mean_mape drops from the ~0.90 standing gap as its level anchor engages — watch dist_insulin / dist_lactate / dist_hepatic_output in the cold_model_distillation telemetry (finite and falling over phase 2). STRUCTURAL SIGNAL: aux-signal losses (gut_sweep, ins_sweep, fasting, postprandial, cohort, physiology) should now move COHERENTLY with their configured weights across epochs rather than byte-identically — the weight-erasure ceiling lifting. Watch the logs for [SKIP-NONFINITE] lines: a few isolated skips are the safety net working; persistent skips of the same signal mean that rollout still destabilizes and needs a targeted fix (e.g. saturating the postprandial residual loss) in iter 79. Risks: (R1) the joint clip (norm 10 over ALL aux combined, vs 10 each before) is a NET REDUCTION in per-epoch aux influence — constraints could end up under-trained vs trajectory; if cold-distill/anchor or sweep constraints look weak in the report, raise grad_clip or split a trajectory-vs-aux clip budget in iter 79 (do NOT also change it here — attribution). (R2) accumulation never zeroes grads between aux signals, so any cross-signal grad pollution (e.g. cold-distill's internal embedding-calibration backward) now rides into the joint step exactly as it rode into cold-distill's solo step before — behavior-preserving, but watched. (R3) if the run still NaN-aborts, the abort signal will read 'joint_aux' (combined gradient) or 'trajectory_rollout/window' (main fit) — NOT an aux signal, since those now self-isolate; that localizes the next fix.
